verdicts.typography: Strong typographic hierarchy and mono-label discipline throughout. One minor rhythm issue: the stat strip numbers (8, 8, 3, 6) appear slightly undersized relative to the generous whitespace of their containers, creating a slight visual imbalance in the hero section.
verdicts.color: Flawless execution of the single-accent red constraint. Near-black on white with consistent red usage for emphasis, status indicators, and the 'This System' column. No off-brand colors, no gradients, no shadows. WCAG AA contrast appears solid across all text levels.
verdicts.layout: Excellent grid alignment and whitespace rhythm overall. The hairline borders are clean and consistent. Minor nitpick: in the analysis grid (d4), the red 'THE RESULT' cell (position 5/6) breaks the strict hairline-border discipline by using a solid fill; while intentional, it slightly disrupts the otherwise uniform border-only aesthetic of the component system.
verdicts.components: High-quality component architecture. The matrix table uses clear iconography (solid vs dashed squares) with effective sticky highlighting for the final column. Accordion affordances are clear with chevron indicators. The stat strip is well-proportioned. One observation: the matrix table would benefit from a visible sticky-state indicator or subtle shadow on the first column during horizontal scroll to reinforce its pinned behavior.
verdicts.responsive: Flawless execution across all breakpoints and modes. Mobile layout maintains perfect integrity at 390px with no overflow or clipped text; the wide matrix table handles horizontal scrolling elegantly with a sticky first column for context. Dark mode demonstrates a consistent, high-contrast palette with proper hierarchy and legible typography.

typography: Increase the font size of the stat strip numerals (8, 8, 3, 6) by 10-15% or tighten their container padding to improve visual weight balance against the surrounding whitespace.
layout: Consider replacing the solid red fill on the analysis grid's 'THE RESULT' cell with a red hairline border and tinted background to maintain stricter consistency with the border-only design language used elsewhere.
components: Add a subtle left shadow or border treatment to the matrix table's sticky first column when horizontally scrolled to provide clearer visual feedback that the column is pinned.
